# x86-64 coverage: the baseline general-purpose instructions a user
# program can run (Intel SDM Vol. 1, chapter 5, without the system
# instructions or anything needing a CPUID feature beyond x86-64's
# baseline). Generated by `scripts/x86_coverage_forms.py` from asmjit's
# `db/isa_x86.json` (zlib license, https://github.com/asmjit/asmjit).
#
# A form is the mnemonic plus the kinds of its written operands: `reg`,
# `mem`, `imm`, `rel` (a jump target), and the fixed `cl`, `dx` and `sreg`.
# Operand sizes count as one form, so `add reg, reg` covers 8- to 64-bit
# registers; the sample uses the widest. Samples are NASM syntax.
name: x86-64
reference: baseline general-purpose, user mode
dialect: std.x86_64.nasm
#
# One line per operand form: `x` if it's covered, then the form, then a
# sample of it in the dialect's syntax. A form is covered when its sample
# compiles. `tests/coverage.rs` checks every marker; after changing what's
# supported, run `make coverage` to update them and the coverage tables.
